subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class group authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the feature changes who can invoke agents/tools through Slack and the report itself calls out Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned message, slash, action, audit, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a migration is separately approved.

options.title: Reject private-channel boundary
options.body: Keep explicit channel ID allowlists as the only non-open Slack channel authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer to broader access-control design
options.body: Track the idea under a broader channel authorization model if maintainers want a cross-channel policy instead of a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned message, slash, action, audit, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a migration is separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has recent Slack/config history near the affected authorization paths.
